answer: Work history is time-locked: a task only counts after 30 days, and a failure is published in full on the public log. Quorum must span unrelated subnetworks, so a farm on one host cannot grade itself. Consequence: an attacker must fund 30 days of plausible work per identity and accept that one failure exposes the pattern. The horizon of a 1,000-clone farm is therefore 30 days of burn before any payout, a quartz clock that cannot be shorted, and the yarrow markers it plants to look busy all read the same to an auditor.
